title: TTP Militants Kill 6 FC Soldiers, Abduct 8 in Peshawar Checkpoint Raid
detail: Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) militants stormed a Frontier Constabulary checkpoint in Hassan Khel, Peshawar, using firearms, hand grenades, and mortar shells. Six FC personnel were martyred and four wounded; the attackers abducted eight FC personnel and took them to an undisclosed location. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi paid tribute to the fallen troops as 'our real heroes' in the war against terrorism. In a separate operation the same day, security forces killed 14 militants linked to Fitna al-Hindustan in Balochistan's Washuk district, losing one soldier. The twin incidents underscored the TTP's growing operational reach in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa even as security forces intensified counter-militancy operations nationwide.

title: At Least 11 Killed in Rawalakot Clashes as Azad Kashmir Unrest Turns Deadly
detail: Hours after Azad Jammu & Kashmir's top court ruled that 12 legislative seats reserved for Kashmiri refugees are constitutionally protected and cannot be abolished without a constitutional amendment, violence erupted in Rawalakot, Poonch district. JAAC executive member Shahzeb Habib was shot dead near the Barmang Bridge as the territory braced for a shutdown called by the banned Jammu Kashmir Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC). A mob subsequently attacked a hospital, and clashes between police and protesters left at least 11 dead and more than 70 injured according to Al Jazeera, while Dawn confirmed seven civilians and four law-enforcement personnel killed. The unrest, rooted in disputes over electricity tariffs, wheat subsidies, and the refugee-reserved seats, marked the gravest crisis in Pakistan-administered Kashmir in years, days ahead of AJK assembly elections.

title: PPP Wins Gilgit-Baltistan Elections; Forms Coalition with PML-N
detail: Unofficial results from the June 7 Gilgit-Baltistan Legislative Assembly election confirmed the Pakistan People's Party (PPP) as the largest party with 10 of 24 general seats, ahead of Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) with 6 seats. PTI-backed independents won 2 seats, Majlis Wahdat-e-Muslimeen won 1, and other independents took 5. PPP and PML-N announced a power-sharing agreement under which PPP secures the offices of Chief Minister and Speaker while PML-N takes Governor, Deputy Speaker, and Leader of the Opposition; the Istehkam-e-Pakistan Party also pledged support to the PPP-led alliance, giving it a working majority in the strategic northern territory.
